1	import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
2	import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";
3	
4	/**
5	 * CSP proxy (Next.js 16 renamed Middleware → Proxy) with per-request nonces.
6	 *
7	 * Why nonces + 'strict-dynamic': only scripts that Next.js has explicitly
8	 * tagged with the nonce can run, and any scripts they load inherit trust.
9	 * This keeps a hypothetical injected `<script>` tag from executing even if
10	 * something slipped past markdown sanitization.
11	 *
12	 * Why `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`: Tailwind v4 emits inline styles. Tightening
13	 * to nonces would require rebuilding how Tailwind ships styles in dev and
14	 * SSR. Documented as a deliberate carve-out, not an oversight.
15	 *
16	 * `connect-src 'self'` is sufficient because Anthropic / OpenAlex / OpenRouter
17	 * calls are server-to-server (Next API routes), not browser-to-third-party.
18	 */
19	function buildCsp(nonce: string): string {
20	  const directives = [
21	    "default-src 'self'",
22	    `script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'`,
23	    "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
24	    "img-src 'self' data: blob:",
25	    "font-src 'self' data:",
26	    "connect-src 'self'",
27	    "frame-ancestors 'none'",
28	    "base-uri 'self'",
29	    "object-src 'none'",
30	  ];
31	  return directives.join("; ");
32	}
33	
34	export function proxy(request: NextRequest): NextResponse {
35	  // Generate a fresh nonce per request. crypto.randomUUID and Buffer are both
36	  // available in the Edge runtime that Next proxy runs in.
37	  const nonce = Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString("base64");
38	
39	  // Forward the nonce to server components via a request header so layouts
40	  // can read it via `headers()` and pass it to <Script> tags they render.
41	  const requestHeaders = new Headers(request.headers);
42	  requestHeaders.set("x-nonce", nonce);
43	
44	  const response = NextResponse.next({
45	    request: { headers: requestHeaders },
46	  });
47	  response.headers.set("Content-Security-Policy", buildCsp(nonce));
48	  return response;
49	}

52	  // Apply CSP to page navigations only. Skip API routes (they don't render
53	  // HTML), Next's static assets (no scripts to nonce), and prefetches (which
54	  // would otherwise burn a nonce on a request that may never paint).

docs/spikes/zustand-state-management.md:11:Yes. Zustand v5 handles all integration points cleanly. The `persist` middleware replaces the manual debounce/localStorage logic. The `getState()` pattern eliminates the stale-closure ref hacks used by `useFormalizationPipeline`. Artifact versioning (undo/redo/edit history) works as a thin layer within the store. SSR hydration is handled via `skipHydration: true` + `rehydrate()` in a useEffect.
docs/spikes/zustand-state-management.md:16:- **persist middleware** replaces the entire `scheduleSave`/`flushSave`/`buildSaveInput` pattern in `useWorkspacePersistence.ts`. `partialize` keeps functions out of localStorage. `skipHydration` is SSR-safe.
docs/spikes/zustand-state-management.md:25:- **Zustand v5 changed `subscribe` API**: Selector-based subscribe (for vanilla JS, not React) requires `subscribeWithSelector` middleware. Not an issue for React components which use `useStore(selector)` instead.
docs/spikes/zustand-state-management.md:29:- **persist middleware saves synchronously on every `set()` call** by default. During streaming (50ms throttled token callbacks), this would write to localStorage on every token. Solutions: (a) use a custom `storage` adapter with debouncing, (b) keep streaming state outside the persisted store (recommended — streaming is transient).
docs/spikes/zustand-state-management.md:55:  - Zustand's persist middleware saves on every `set()` — debounce or exclude transient state.
docs/spikes/zustand-state-management.md:58:  - The `flushSave()` pattern (used after generation completes) is handled naturally by persist middleware — but if debouncing is added, need an explicit flush mechanism.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	Metaformalism Copilot is a Next.js web app for transforming insights and source material into personalized, context-sensitive formalisms. It's part of the [Live Conversational Threads](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/uueHkKrGmeEsKGHPR/live-conversational-threads-not-an-ai-notetaker-2) research project. The philosophy ("Live Theory") emphasizes generalization via inclusion — producing multiple rigorous representations tailored to specific contexts rather than a single unified theory.
8	
9	## Prerequisites
10	
11	- Node.js (v18+) and npm
12	- An `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable for LLM features
13	
14	## Commands
15	
16	All commands run from the repo root:
17	
18	```bash
19	npm run dev        # Start dev server at localhost:3000
20	npm run build      # Production build
21	npm run lint       # ESLint (eslint-config-next with core-web-vitals + typescript)
22	npm test           # Run tests (Vitest)
23	npm run test:watch # Run tests in watch mode
24	npm run test:ui    # Run tests with Vitest UI
25	```
26	
27	## Architecture
28	
29	The app is a **multi-panel workspace** with a collapsible Icon Rail sidebar for navigation. The root `page.tsx` orchestrates all state and renders the active panel via a `PanelShell` layout. State is persisted to localStorage via `useWorkspacePersistence` and survives page refreshes.
30	
31	### Directory Layout (under `app/`)
32	
33	- `page.tsx` — Root orchestrator: manages panel navigation, all workspace state, and delegates to panel components
34	- `layout.tsx` — Sets up fonts (EB Garamond serif + Geist Mono) and metadata
35	- `globals.css` — CSS variables (`--ivory-cream`, `--ink-black`, `--paper-shadow`) and Tailwind v4 config via `@theme inline`
36	- `components/layout/` — `PanelShell` (Icon Rail + focus pane layout), `IconRail` (sidebar navigation)
37	- `components/panels/` — One component per panel: `InputPanel`, `SemiformalPanel`, `LeanPanel`, `GraphPanel`, `NodeDetailPanel`, `CausalGraphPanel`, `StatisticalModelPanel`, `PropertyTestsPanel`, `DialecticalMapPanel`, `AnalyticsPanel`
38	- `components/features/` — Feature modules organized by domain:
39	  - `source-input/` — `TextInput`, `FileUpload` (.txt, .doc, .docx, .pdf)
40	  - `context-input/` — `ContextInput`, `RefinementButtons`, `RefinementPreview`
41	  - `output-editing/` — `EditableOutput`; `ai-bars/InlineEditPopup` (Cmd+K) and `ai-bars/WholeTextEditBar`
42	  - `workspace-session/` — `WorkspaceSessionBar` for session switching
43	  - `session-banner/` — `SessionBanner` for per-panel session context
44	  - `artifact-selector/` — Artifact type selection UI
45	  - `causal-graph/` — Graph visualization components
46	  - `lean-display/` — Lean code display with syntax highlighting
47	- `components/ui/` — Shared UI components and icons
48	- `hooks/` — Custom hooks: `useWorkspacePersistence`, `useWorkspaceSessions`, `useFormalizationPipeline`, `useDecomposition`, `useAutoFormalizeQueue`, `useAnalytics`, etc.
49	- `lib/types/` — TypeScript type definitions for panels, sessions, artifacts, decomposition
50	- `lib/llm/` — LLM integration (Anthropic SDK, schemas, caching)
51	- `lib/formalization/` — Shared artifact generation logic
52	- `lib/utils/` — Utilities (PDF parsing, LaTeX parsing, export, text selection)
53	- `api/` — Next.js API routes for formalization, editing, verification, decomposition, analytics
54	
55	### Key Patterns
56	
57	- **Feature-based folder structure**: components grouped by feature domain, not by type
58	- **Import alias**: `@/*` maps to the project root (configured in `tsconfig.json`)
59	- **Client components**: Panel components use `"use client"` since they manage state
60	- **Multiple artifact types**: semiformal, lean, causal-graph, statistical-model, property-tests, dialectical-map — each with a dedicated panel and API route
61	- **Decomposition workflow**: extract propositions from sources into a dependency graph, then formalize per-node
62	- **Session management**: workspace sessions (global) and formalization sessions (per-scope) for tracking artifact history
63	
64	### Design System
65	
66	- CSS variables in `globals.css` are the source of truth for theming
67	- Tailwind CSS v4 with `@tailwindcss/postcss`
68	- Primary font: EB Garamond (serif); Mono: Geist Mono
69	- Styling uses both Tailwind classes and `var(--css-variable)` references
70	
71	## Code Guidelines
72	
73	- TypeScript for all components
74	- Tailwind CSS for styling; theme colors via CSS variables in `globals.css`
75	- Components should be modular and single-responsibility
76	- Follow existing feature-based folder structure in `app/components/features/`
77	- Ensure `npm run lint` passes before committing
78	
79	## Git Workflow
80	
81	- Always work on feature branches, never commit directly to main
82	- Commit after each logical unit of work with conventional commit messages (feat:, fix:, refactor:, test:, docs:)
83	- Push the branch after each commit so work is backed up remotely
84	- Before finishing a session, ensure all work is committed and pushed
85	- When asked to prepare for review, do an interactive rebase to clean up WIP commits into logical chunks
86	
87	## Code Quality
88	
89	- Tests use Vitest with React Testing Library. Write tests alongside implementation.
90	- Add comments explaining "why" for non-obvious library usage or architectural choices
91	- When choosing a new library or significant architectural approach, create a short decision record in `docs/decisions/NNN-title.md` explaining what was chosen and why
92	
93	## Documentation Maintenance
94	
95	When making changes that affect user-facing behavior, project structure, or available commands, check whether the following docs need updating:
96	
97	- `README.md` — UI description, available scripts, prerequisites, project documentation links
98	- `CLAUDE.md` — Architecture section, directory layout, commands, key patterns
99	- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — Component hierarchy and technical details
100	- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — Project structure section, code guidelines
101	
102	If a PR adds a new panel, artifact type, API route, script, or dependency, update the relevant docs in the same PR.
103	
104	## PR Preparation
105	
106	- Generate detailed PR descriptions including: summary of changes, motivation/context, how to test, and areas of uncertainty or risk
107	- Flag sections where you used unfamiliar libraries or patterns that the reviewer should scrutinize
108	- Note which tests (if any) cover which functionality
109	- Keep PRs to one reviewable concept; prefer multiple smaller PRs over one large one

# 005: Streaming API Responses

## Context

The app makes LLM calls that take 15-85 seconds. A wait-time estimation system was built (PR pending) using hardcoded regression priors, but the estimates were often 3x off (e.g., 25s predicted vs 75s actual for causal-graph). Rather than improving the prediction model, streaming solves the root cause by showing real progress.

## Decision

Replace batch LLM responses with streaming across all API routes. Two phases:

### Phase 1: Stream raw tokens, render on completion
- Stream tokens from the LLM to the client via SSE
- Display raw streaming text as a loading preview for all artifact types
- On stream completion, parse and render the final visualization (for JSON artifacts) or display the final text (for text artifacts)
- This gives immediate visual feedback without requiring partial JSON parsing

### Phase 2: Partial JSON rendering
- Use a partial JSON parser client-side to progressively render JSON visualizations as tokens arrive
- E.g., show causal graph nodes as they appear in the stream, before edges are complete
- Only attempted after Phase 1 is stable

## Alternatives considered
- **Improved wait-time prediction** (Bayesian updating, EMA) — still guessing; doesn't solve the fundamental problem
- **Summary-first prompting** — adds output tokens (cost), and a text summary isn't useful loading UI for graph visualizations
- **Two-phase (text then JSON)** — doubles latency

Diff reviewed, both files read, and I confirmed how Next actually derives the script nonce (`/repo/node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/app-render.js:166-167` reads `content-security-policy` off the **incoming request** headers, then `get-script-nonce-from-header.js` parses the `'nonce-…'` source out of `script-src`).

Findings (Simplification angle)

1. **proxy.ts:42** — `x-nonce` is written onto the forwarded request headers but nothing in the app ever reads it; the header Next needs on the request is `Content-Security-Policy`, not `x-nonce`.
   *failure_scenario*: A grep for `x-nonce` across `/repo/app` returns only the comment in `layout.tsx` that says it deliberately doesn't read it — so the header, the `new Headers(request.headers)` clone, and the `request: { headers }` option on `NextResponse.next` are all pure ceremony that a future reader must trace before deleting. Worse, the tension is real and resolves the other way: Next reads the nonce from the *request's* `content-security-policy` header, and this diff sets CSP only on the *response*, so Next's bootstrap `<script>` tags render un-nonced and `'strict-dynamic'` blocks all app JS. The simpler form is one line that is both shorter and correct — compute `const csp = buildCsp(nonce)`, then `requestHeaders.set("Content-Security-Policy", csp)` alongside `response.headers.set("Content-Security-Policy", csp)` — and drop `x-nonce` entirely.

2. **proxy.ts:37** — `Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString("base64")` wraps a value that is already a valid CSP nonce.
   *failure_scenario*: A UUID is hex plus hyphens, entirely inside the `base64-value` grammar CSP requires, so the Buffer round-trip only lengthens the string (36 → 48 chars) while dragging the Node `Buffer` global into the Edge runtime — which in turn is the *only* reason the two-line comment at lines 35-36 ("`Buffer` is available in the Edge runtime") has to exist. Anyone later porting this proxy to a stricter runtime, or auditing which Node polyfills the edge bundle pulls in, pays to re-derive that this was never needed. Simpler form: `const nonce = crypto.randomUUID();`, deleting the justification comment with it (Next's own docs use `btoa(crypto.randomUUID())` if a base64 shape is wanted, with no `Buffer`).

3. **app/layout.tsx:31** — `await headers()` with a discarded result is an obscure spelling of "force dynamic", and it forces `RootLayout` to become `async`.
   *failure_scenario*: A bare `await headers();` with no assignment reads as a leftover and is exactly the kind of statement a lint rule, a formatter cleanup, or a future contributor deletes as dead — silently re-enabling static prerendering of the layout, which bakes one build-time nonce into the HTML for all users and breaks CSP for everyone. The three-line comment exists solely to defend the line against that deletion. Simpler and self-documenting: `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";` at module scope, which states the intent in the framework's own vocabulary, keeps `RootLayout` a plain sync function, and drops the `next/headers` import added at line 3.

4. **app/layout.tsx:28-30** — the comment asserts a mechanism that does not exist ("Next.js automatically tags its own bootstrap `<script>` elements with the nonce from the **response's** CSP header").
   *failure_scenario*: Next reads the nonce from the request headers (app-render.js:166), so this comment actively teaches the wrong model and will send the next person debugging blocked scripts to look at the browser's response headers, where everything appears correct. Once finding 1 is applied the comment becomes both true and unnecessary, and can shrink to a one-liner pointing at `proxy.ts`.

5. **proxy.ts:19-32** — `buildCsp` is a per-request function allocating a 9-element array in which 8 entries are compile-time constants, called from exactly one place (line 47).
   *failure_scenario*: Every request allocates and joins an array to vary a single substring, and the constant policy is split across a helper so that changing a directive means reading a function signature, an array, and a `.join` to confirm the separator. Simpler: hoist the invariant text to a module-level `const` and return a template literal, e.g. a single `` `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'; …` `` — same output, no helper indirection, no per-request array.

6. **proxy.ts:16-17** — the `connect-src` rationale comment names OpenAlex, which appears nowhere in the repo.
   *failure_scenario*: `grep -rniE "openalex"` over the tree (excluding `node_modules`) matches only `proxy.ts` itself; Anthropic (`/repo/app/lib/llm/callLlm.ts`) and OpenRouter (`/repo/app/lib/llm/callLlm.ts`, `/repo/app/lib/formalization/artifactRoute.ts`, several `/repo/app/api/**/route.ts`) are real, OpenAlex is not. A future reviewer tightening or widening `connect-src` will go hunting for an OpenAlex integration that was never built, or will assume the comment is authoritative and preserve an allowance for it. Simpler: name only the two services that exist, or drop the enumeration and keep the invariant that matters ("all LLM calls are server-side via `/api/*`").

Secondary note (not counted, adjacent to finding 1): the `missing` prefetch exclusion at proxy.ts:57-60 is justified by "would otherwise burn a nonce," but nonces have no cost to generate, so the exclusion buys nothing while leaving prefetched navigations without a CSP header — deleting the `missing` block makes the matcher a plain string and removes the object form entirely.

Findings from `git diff main...HEAD` (commits 9b4e453, b25e939, d90d6bb):

**1. /repo/proxy.ts:47 — CSP is set only on the response; Next reads the nonce from the *request* CSP header, so the nonce scheme never engages.**
`response.headers.set("Content-Security-Policy", ...)` is the only place the policy is written. Next's app renderer sources the nonce at `/repo/node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/app-render.js:166-167` — it reads `headers['content-security-policy']` from the *incoming request* headers and runs `getScriptNonceFromHeader` on it. `requestHeaders` here only ever gets `x-nonce`, never the CSP. failure_scenario: Next's bootstrap/hydration `<script>` tags render with no `nonce` attribute while the browser enforces `script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'`; because `'strict-dynamic'` causes conformant browsers to ignore `'self'`, *every* script is blocked and the app ships as a dead, unhydrated shell — a failure that only appears in a real browser, not in unit tests or `next build`. The deeper fix is to set the built CSP string on `requestHeaders` as well as the response (the shape Next's own docs prescribe), so the nonce has exactly one source of truth that both the renderer and the browser see.

**2. /repo/app/layout.tsx:31 — `await headers()` result is discarded; dynamic rendering rests on an invisible side effect.**
The call exists purely to trip Next's dynamic-API detection, with the intent carried only by the comment above it. failure_scenario: any lint pass, "remove unused await" cleanup, or a maintainer converting the component back to non-async silently restores static rendering — the layout is then generated at build time with one baked-in nonce (or none), and the per-request CSP quietly stops matching the served HTML, with no test or type error to catch it. The self-documenting fix is `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` at module scope, which states the requirement as configuration rather than as a load-bearing no-op, or — better — actually reading the nonce (finding 4) so the value is genuinely used and cannot be deleted without a compile error.

**3. /repo/app/layout.tsx:28-30 — the explanatory comment states a mechanism that does not exist, entrenching finding 1.**
"Next.js automatically tags its own bootstrap `<script>` elements with the nonce from the response's CSP header, so we don't need to read x-nonce here ourselves" is factually inverted (Next reads the request header). failure_scenario: this comment is the exact artifact a future debugger will consult when scripts start getting blocked; it confidently redirects them away from the real bug and toward blaming the browser or the matcher, converting a five-line fix into a multi-hour investigation. Comments asserting framework behavior at this depth need either a doc link or a test pinning the behavior.

**4. /repo/proxy.ts:39-42 — `x-nonce` is forwarded to server components but has zero readers; the design is split-brain.**
`grep -rn "x-nonce" /repo/app` returns nothing but the layout comment saying it is deliberately *not* read, and there are no `<Script>`, `<script>`, or `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` usages anywhere in `/repo/app`. failure_scenario: the header is dead-by-design plumbing that reads as working infrastructure — the next person adding an inline analytics or theme-flash script will assume nonces are wired end-to-end, ship a script with no `nonce` attribute, and have it silently blocked in production only. Either complete the wiring (layout reads `(await headers()).get("x-nonce")` and threads it to the scripts that need it, which also resolves finding 2) or drop the header and its comment so the file describes what it actually does.

**5. /repo/proxy.ts:5-17 — CSP rationale lives only in file comments; /repo/docs/decisions has no record, contrary to the repo's own convention.**
`/repo/CLAUDE.md:91` requires a `docs/decisions/NNN-title.md` record for "significant architectural approach", and `/repo/docs/decisions` holds eight ADRs for comparably scoped choices (state management, streaming). The `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` Tailwind carve-out, the `'strict-dynamic'` trust model, and the `connect-src 'self'` server-to-server argument are exactly the kind of reasoning ADRs exist to preserve. failure_scenario: this branch already demonstrates the decay — commit b25e939 was a fix for a comment that went stale when middleware was renamed to proxy. When the file is next renamed, split per-route, or replaced by `next.config.ts` headers, the security reasoning (especially *why* `unsafe-inline` is acceptable) evaporates with it, and a future maintainer either re-litigates it or tightens/loosens it blindly.

**6. /repo/proxy.ts:51-63 — no test or verification anywhere for a security-critical, browser-only behavior.**
There is no `proxy.test.ts` and no test referencing `Content-Security-Policy` in the repo, despite Vitest being configured. failure_scenario: findings 1 and 2 are both classes of bug that are invisible to every existing check and only surface as a blank page in production; the matcher's prefetch exclusion has the same property (a document served on a prefetch path gets no CSP header at all). A test asserting that `proxy()` puts the same nonce into both the request `content-security-policy` header and the response header — plus one asserting the rendered HTML's script tags carry it — is what turns this from an unfalsifiable comment-based design into an enforced one.

Diff read. App shape: exactly **one** page route (`/repo/app/page.tsx`, `"use client"`, 807 lines, ~15 panel components) plus 17 API routes (matcher-excluded and inherently dynamic already). No `next/link` anywhere, no `next/script`, no `export const dynamic/revalidate`, empty `next.config.ts`.

Findings (efficiency angle, highest-cost first):

1. **/repo/proxy.ts:41-47** — The entire per-request nonce pipeline is dead work: the nonce never reaches a consumer. Next.js stamps its bootstrap `<script>` tags by reading the nonce from the **request's** `Content-Security-Policy` header (the one passed through `NextResponse.next({ request: { headers } })`), not from the response header. Here only `x-nonce` is set on the request, and `grep` confirms nothing in `/repo/app` ever reads `x-nonce`; the CSP string is set only on the response.
   *failure_scenario:* Every request pays `randomUUID` + base64 + a full `Headers` clone + a forced dynamic render, and produces a nonce that zero scripts carry — 100% wasted. Worse, `'strict-dynamic'` then blocks every un-nonced Next bootstrap script, so the page ships HTML and hydrates nothing (blank/dead UI) while still paying the full dynamic-render cost. Cheaper: add `requestHeaders.set("Content-Security-Policy", csp)` so the work is at least consumed — or delete the nonce path per #2 and pay nothing.

2. **/repo/app/layout.tsx:31** — `await headers()` in the root layout opts the app's *only* user-facing route out of static rendering and full-route caching. `app/page.tsx` is a client component, which Next still prerenders to a static HTML shell at build time; that shell is now re-rendered on the server for every single page view, and the route can no longer be served from the full-route/CDN cache.
   *failure_scenario:* Under any traffic, every hit re-runs the 807-line client tree's server pass (~15 panel component modules) instead of returning a cached prebuilt shell — turning a zero-compute CDN hit into an origin render, with the corresponding TTFB and cost increase, for the single route that is 100% of page views. The nonce approach does inherently require dynamic rendering, but a cheaper alternative fits here: this app has no `next/script`, no third-party inline scripts, and only client-rendered content, so the CSP can be emitted as a static header from `next.config.ts` `headers()` (hash-based or nonce-free). That costs zero per-request work, skips proxy invocation on the document entirely, and keeps the route prerendered.

3. **/repo/proxy.ts:57** — Matcher regex `/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)` still matches `/public` assets and RSC/data requests. `/repo/public` contains `file.svg`, `globe.svg`, `next.svg`, `vercel.svg`, `window.svg`, and `_next/data` / RSC payload fetches are not excluded either.
   *failure_scenario:* The proxy boots and runs the nonce + header-clone path for asset and non-HTML requests, stamping a `Content-Security-Policy` header on responses no browser enforces it on — pure waste, though small in absolute terms (5 static assets, low request volume). Cheaper: append a file-extension negative lookahead, e.g. `(?!api|_next|favicon.ico|.*\\.(?:svg|png|ico|txt|xml)$).*`.

I searched for every pre-existing place this repo could already be setting security headers, and found **none**:

- `/repo/next.config.ts` — 7 lines, completely empty config object. No `headers()`, no `poweredByHeader`, nothing.
- No `vercel.json`, `netlify.toml`, `_headers`, `nginx.conf`, or `Caddyfile` anywhere in the tree.
- `/repo/docker-compose.yml` only defines the `lean-verifier` Go/Lean sidecar on :3100 — no reverse proxy in front of Next.
- No pre-existing `middleware.ts` / `proxy.ts` remnant; `proxy.ts` is the only match for `find -iname "middleware*" -o -iname "proxy*"`.
- Zero hits repo-wide (excluding `node_modules`/`.next`) for `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Strict-Transport-Security`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`, or `frame-ancestors` outside the new `proxy.ts`.
- Zero hits for `headers.set` / `new Headers` / `NextResponse.next` in `app/`, `scripts/`, `verifier/` — the 20+ API routes never touch response headers.
- `/repo/package.json` carries no `helmet`, `next-safe`, `@next-safe/middleware`, `next-secure-headers`, or similar. Nothing already provides this.

So: no *existing security-header mechanism* is duplicated or conflicted with. The reuse findings below are about the new code re-implementing Next.js primitives and about internal duplication within the diff itself.

## Findings

1. **`/repo/app/layout.tsx:31** — `await headers()` is used purely as a side effect to force dynamic rendering, re-implementing Next's existing declarative primitive `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`.
   *failure_scenario:* The call has no return value, no consumer, and a comment as its only justification. Any lint pass, refactor, or "remove unused await" cleanup deletes it; the root layout silently reverts to static prerendering, the proxy's per-request nonce no longer matches the prerendered HTML's bootstrap scripts, and every page ships a `script-src 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'` header whose nonce tags nothing — the app renders a blank page in production while working fine in `next dev`. The already-supported route-segment config expresses the same intent in a form that cannot be accidentally optimized away.

2. **`/repo/proxy.ts:39-45** — the `x-nonce` request-header forwarding is dead code with zero readers; the diff builds a second nonce-delivery channel it then declares unnecessary.
   *failure_scenario:* `grep -rn "x-nonce"` over the whole repo returns exactly two hits: the `requestHeaders.set` in proxy.ts and the layout comment saying "we don't need to read x-nonce here ourselves." Cloning `request.headers` into a fresh `Headers` and re-issuing the request through `NextResponse.next({ request })` on every navigation buys nothing today, and establishes two sources of truth. The next developer who adds a `<Script>` reads `x-nonce` in a route the matcher excludes (`/api/*`, or any prefetch, which the `missing:` clause deliberately skips) and gets `null` → either a crashing `nonce={null!}` or a script silently blocked by the very CSP this file installs.

3. **`/repo/proxy.ts:37** — `Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString("base64")` re-implements nonce generation via the Node `Buffer` shim when Web Crypto + `btoa` are the native Edge primitives, and diverges from the repo's own established `crypto.randomUUID()` usage.
   *failure_scenario:* `Buffer` in Next's proxy runtime exists only because Next polyfills it; on any deploy target that runs proxy code on a stricter Edge/Workers runtime (or if Next drops the shim), this throws `ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined` on the very first request — and because it is in the proxy, *every* page 500s, not just one route. 4. **`/repo/proxy.ts:20-30 (directives array)** — the seven fully static directives (`default-src`, `style-src`, `img-src`, `font-src`, `connect-src`, `frame-ancestors`, `base-uri`, `object-src`) are recomputed and re-serialized per request inside `buildCsp(nonce)`, bypassing `next.config.ts`'s existing `headers()` surface which is built for exactly this.
   *failure_scenario:* Only `script-src` actually depends on the nonce. 5. **`/repo/proxy.ts:22 vs. `/repo/app/lib/utils/pdfPropositionParser.ts:443** — `script-src 'strict-dynamic'` overrides the `'self'` allowlist, which conflicts with the repo's existing same-origin pdf.js web-worker load.

6. **`/repo/proxy.ts:14** — the `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` carve-out is justified by Tailwind, but the repo's `html-to-image` export path is the load-bearing consumer and is undocumented.
   *failure_scenario:* `/repo/app/lib/utils/exportGraph.ts` uses `html-to-image` (package.json `^1.11.13`), which inlines computed styles into an SVG `foreignObject` and serializes to a data URL. A future hardening pass reads the comment, concludes "Tailwind v4 no longer needs this in v5," tightens `style-src` to nonces, and graph PNG/SVG export breaks silently — the carve-out's stated rationale doesn't name the dependency that actually pins it.

## Findings

**1. `proxy.ts:41-47` — CSP header is never set on the *forwarded request* headers, so Next.js never learns the nonce and blocks its own scripts.**
Next 16 extracts the nonce from the **incoming request's** CSP header, not the response's. Confirmed in the installed framework: `node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/app-render.js:166` inside `parseRequestHeaders(headers, …)` does `const csp = headers['content-security-policy'] || headers['content-security-policy-report-only']` and then `getScriptNonceFromHeader(csp)`. The official guide's example sets it in both places (`requestHeaders.set('Content-Security-Policy', …)` *and* `response.headers.set(…)`); this diff only sets the response one.
failure_scenario: `next build && next start`, browser GET `/` → proxy emits `script-src 'self' 'nonce-ABC' 'strict-dynamic'` on the response, but SSR renders every `<script>` (framework bootstrap, `self.__next_f.push(...)` inline flight chunks, page bundles) with **no** `nonce` attribute. Because `'strict-dynamic'` causes the browser to ignore host-sources including `'self'`, all of those scripts are refused → white page, zero hydration, console full of "Refused to execute inline script". The app is fully broken in production, not just partially.

**2. `app/layout.tsx:27-31` — the new comment states the mechanism backwards, and `await headers()` is not sufficient to get nonces applied.**
"Next.js automatically tags its own bootstrap `<script>` elements with the nonce from the response's CSP header" is false per finding 1 (request header). Also, `x-nonce` is set in `proxy.ts:42` but read by nobody in the repo (`grep` shows no consumer), so the only nonce channel that exists is the one the framework can't see.
failure_scenario: A future maintainer trusts the comment, keeps `await headers()` and never adds the request-header CSP, so the layout pays the full cost of opting the entire route tree out of static rendering (every request now SSRs, no CDN caching, PPR incompatible) while gaining zero nonce coverage — a pure regression: slower *and* still CSP-broken.

**3. `proxy.ts:22` — no development carve-out for `'unsafe-eval'` (and `NODE_ENV` is never consulted).**
The Next.js CSP guide explicitly states: "In development, `'unsafe-eval'` is required because React uses `eval` to provide enhanced debugging information, such as reconstructing server-side error stacks in the browser."
failure_scenario: `npm run dev`, open `http://localhost:3000`, edit any component under `app/components/` → the react-refresh / dev-overlay code paths that call `eval`/`new Function` are blocked ("Refused to evaluate a string as JavaScript because 'unsafe-eval' is not an allowed source"). Confirmed the mechanism in Next 16.2.4's source. Here are my findings.

## Findings

**1. `proxy.ts:47` (with `proxy.ts:42`) — CSP is set only on the *response*; Next.js reads the nonce from the *request* headers, so no script ever gets nonced.**
`/repo/node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/app-render.js:166` is inside `parseRequestHeaders(headers, options)` and does `const csp = headers['content-security-policy'] || headers['content-security-policy-report-only']` — those are the *incoming request* headers. The proxy forwards only `x-nonce` on `requestHeaders` and sets `Content-Security-Policy` on `response.headers`. Next's documented recipe requires setting the CSP header on **both**. Result: `nonce` is `undefined` during app-render, and Next emits its bootstrap `<script>` tags with no `nonce` attribute.
*failure_scenario*: On the first page load of `/`, the browser receives `script-src 'self' 'nonce-XYZ' 'strict-dynamic'`. Under CSP Level 3, the presence of `'strict-dynamic'` causes `'self'` to be **ignored**, and the un-nonced `/_next/static/chunks/*.js` bootstrap scripts are all blocked. `app/page.tsx` is `"use client"` with all interactivity in hooks, so the user sees a dead, never-hydrated shell — no panels respond, no state, console full of CSP violations. This ships as a total app outage, not a hardening win.

**2. `app/layout.tsx:22` — removed behavior: `export default function RootLayout` → `async` + `await headers()` disables static prerendering for every route in the app, and buys nothing in exchange.**
`grep -rn "generateStaticParams|force-static|revalidate|export const dynamic" /repo/app` returns **zero** matches — no route ever opted into or out of anything, so `/` (the only page, `app/page.tsx`) was prerendered at build time as `○ Static`. Because this is the *root* layout, the dynamic opt-out is inherited by the entire tree, present and future.
*failure_scenario*: `next build` output for `/` flips from `○ (Static)` to `ƒ (Dynamic)`; `.next/server/app/index.html` is no longer emitted. Every visit now pays a full server render of the root layout + client-component shell instead of being served from the prerender/CDN full-route cache, adding TTFB on every cold hit and removing the ability to serve the shell while the origin is down. Nothing in the repo re-establishes static rendering — no `export const dynamic = "force-static"`, no PPR (`next.config.ts` is empty), no `revalidate`. Note this is not a *build failure* (there is no `output: "export"` in `/repo/next.config.ts`), so CI's `npm run build` step stays green and the regression ships silently.

**3. `app/layout.tsx:27` — the justifying comment states the wrong mechanism, so the cost/benefit that motivated deleting the sync signature is not real.**
The comment says "Opt this layout out of static rendering **so proxy.ts runs on every request**." Proxy/middleware already runs on every matching request regardless of whether the route is statically prerendered — that is the entire point of middleware sitting in front of the cache. The dynamic opt-out is only needed so the *rendered HTML* can embed a per-request nonce, and per finding 1 the HTML never embeds one. So the app-wide loss of static rendering is currently paid for zero benefit.

**4. `proxy.ts:42` — `x-nonce` is forwarded to server components but nothing reads it; the layout comment explicitly declines to.**
`grep -rn "x-nonce" /repo --exclude-dir=node_modules` matches only `proxy.ts:42` (the write) and `app/layout.tsx:30` (a comment saying "we don't need to read x-nonce here ourselves"). This is the safety net that would have made the design work if the header-name detail in finding 1 were wrong, and it is unused.
*failure_scenario*: A future contributor adds a `<Script>` or inline `<script>` to the layout, sees `x-nonce` being set in the proxy, and assumes nonces are wired up — but there is no plumbing, and per finding 1 no framework-level nonce either, so their script is silently blocked in production while working fine in any environment where the proxy is bypassed.

**5. `proxy.ts:56-62` — the `missing:` prefetch exclusion means some HTML document responses are served with no CSP header at all.**
The matcher skips any request carrying `next-router-prefetch` or `purpose: prefetch`. Browser-initiated speculation-rules prerenders and some CDN/prefetch intermediaries send `purpose: prefetch` on a **document** request, not just on RSC payload fetches.
*failure_scenario*: A prerendered navigation is committed by the browser and the resulting document — a real, script-executing page — was delivered with zero `Content-Security-Policy`, silently un-hardened. The comment's rationale ("would otherwise burn a nonce on a request that may never paint") describes a non-cost: nonces are generated per-request and free.

**6. `proxy.ts:37` — `Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString("base64")` (low confidence / style).**
`Buffer` is polyfilled in Next's edge runtime so this does run, but base64-encoding a UUID string yields ~48 bytes of encoded ASCII hex carrying only 122 bits of entropy, and the dependency on a runtime polyfill is unnecessary when `btoa`/`crypto.getRandomValues` are native to the Edge runtime. Not a security break, just avoidable coupling.

## On "did anything rely on RootLayout being sync?"
No. I checked: no test file imports `app/layout.tsx` (`grep -rln layout` across `*.test.tsx` returns nothing), the `next/font/google` calls and `export const metadata` are module-scope and unaffected by the signature change, and there are no other layouts or `template.tsx` files. The async conversion itself is safe — the damage is entirely the dynamic-rendering opt-out (finding 2) and the fact that the CSP it enables is misconfigured (finding 1).

**Bottom line:** findings 1 and 2 compound badly — the branch gives up app-wide static rendering in order to inject a nonce that never reaches the HTML, and the resulting `'strict-dynamic'` policy blocks all of Next's own scripts. I'd treat finding 1 as a release blocker.

content.text: All key claims verified. Consolidating the eight finders' reports, deduplicating, and reporting the verified findings.

findings.summary: The CSP is set only on the response, but Next.js reads the script nonce from the incoming request's Content-Security-Policy header (node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/app-render.js:166), so no rendered script ever carries the nonce and 'strict-dynamic' causes browsers to ignore 'self', blocking every script.
findings.failure_scenario: In `next build && next start`, a browser loads `/`: the response carries `script-src 'self' 'nonce-X' 'strict-dynamic'`, but every bootstrap and flight `<script>` renders without a nonce attribute. Since 'strict-dynamic' makes the browser ignore 'self', all scripts are refused — the app ships as a dead, never-hydrated HTML shell on 100% of requests. Fix per Next's own CSP guide: also `requestHeaders.set("Content-Security-Policy", csp)` before `NextResponse.next()`.
findings.short_summary: CSP never set on request headers; nonce unused, all JS blocked

findings.summary: The comment claims Next.js tags its bootstrap scripts "with the nonce from the response's CSP header" — the mechanism is inverted (Next reads the request header), and this wrong comment is what conceals the blank-page bug.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer debugging blocked scripts trusts the comment, checks the browser's response headers (which look correct), and never finds the real cause: the nonce is parsed from request headers the proxy never sets. The comment should state the request-header mechanism and point at proxy.ts.
findings.short_summary: Layout comment states the nonce mechanism backwards

findings.summary: `connect-src 'self'` blocks the `fetch(dataUrl)` calls in app/lib/utils/exportGraph.ts:24 and :37, silently breaking graph PNG export and the zip export's embedded graph image.
findings.failure_scenario: User clicks "Export .png" in GraphPanel: `toPng` returns a `data:image/png` URL, `fetch(dataUrl)` is governed by connect-src, and `'self'` does not match the `data:` scheme — the fetch throws, the catch logs `[graph export]`, and no file downloads with no visible error. Fix in app code (use html-to-image's `toBlob` instead of `toPng`+`fetch`) or add `data:` to connect-src.
findings.short_summary: connect-src 'self' breaks graph PNG export fetch(data:)

findings.summary: The `missing` matcher conditions skip the proxy for any request carrying `purpose: prefetch` or `next-router-prefetch`, so a prefetched document response is served with no CSP header at all.
findings.failure_scenario: A browser speculative prefetch (Chrome sends `purpose: prefetch`) or any intermediary that adds that header fetches a full document; the HTML is cached and later committed as the real navigation with zero Content-Security-Policy — the markdown-injection scenario the file header cites runs unblocked. The stated rationale ("burn a nonce") is a non-cost; drop the `missing` block and use a plain string matcher.
findings.short_summary: Prefetch exclusion serves documents with no CSP at all

findings.summary: No development carve-out for `'unsafe-eval'`: Next's CSP guide states React needs eval in dev for error-stack reconstruction, so `npm run dev` gets a broken dev overlay and failing HMR paths on every developer machine.
findings.failure_scenario: Developer runs `npm run dev`, edits a component: react-refresh/dev-overlay code calling `eval`/`new Function` is refused ("Refused to evaluate a string as JavaScript"); the error overlay renders blank and HMR updates stop applying. Standard fix: include `'unsafe-eval'` in script-src when `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'`.
findings.short_summary: No dev 'unsafe-eval' carve-out; breaks dev overlay/HMR

findings.summary: No `worker-src` (and no `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`) directive, so pdfjs's `new Worker(...)` and its WebAssembly image decoders depend on the worker-src→script-src fallback interacting with 'strict-dynamic' — a corner where browser engines have diverged.
findings.failure_scenario: User uploads a PDF via FileUpload: in an engine that blocks the un-nonced worker request under 'strict-dynamic' (or blocks `WebAssembly.instantiate` for JPX/JBIG2-containing PDFs without 'wasm-unsafe-eval'), `extractTextFromPDF` rejects or silently degrades to the main-thread fake worker — PDF ingestion fails or freezes while DOCX/text work, and no test catches it because fileExtraction.test.ts mocks pdfjs-dist. Adding `worker-src 'self' blob:` (and `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`) removes the ambiguity.
findings.short_summary: Missing worker-src/wasm-unsafe-eval risks PDF extraction

findings.summary: A bare `await headers()` with a discarded result is an obscure, deletion-prone spelling of "force dynamic rendering" — `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` states the same intent declaratively and keeps RootLayout sync.
findings.failure_scenario: A future cleanup (lint rule, "remove unused await", de-async refactor) deletes the no-op call; the layout silently reverts to static prerendering, baking one build-time nonce into the HTML for all users while `npm run build` stays green. Note also the cost this line buys: the app's only page loses static prerendering and full-route/CDN caching on every request — inherent to per-request nonces, but worth making explicit and testable rather than a comment-defended side effect.
findings.short_summary: Discarded await headers(); use export const dynamic instead

findings.summary: The `x-nonce` request header has zero readers anywhere in the repo (the only other mention is the layout comment declining to read it), making the header, the Headers clone, and the `request: { headers }` option dead plumbing.
findings.failure_scenario: A future contributor adds an inline `<Script>`, sees `x-nonce` set in the proxy, assumes nonce wiring is end-to-end, and ships a script that is silently blocked in production. Either complete the wiring (read it via `headers()` and thread it to scripts) or delete the header; after fixing the request-CSP bug the forwarded header should carry the CSP string, not `x-nonce`.
findings.short_summary: x-nonce request header is dead code with no readers

findings.summary: `Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString("base64")` wraps a value that is already a valid CSP nonce, inflating it from 36 to 48 chars and pulling the Node Buffer polyfill into the Edge bundle for no entropy gain.
findings.failure_scenario: On a stricter edge runtime without the Buffer shim, every matched request throws `ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined`, 500ing all pages. `const nonce = crypto.randomUUID()` (or `btoa` over getRandomValues bytes) is shorter, native, and matches the repo's existing bare `crypto.randomUUID()` usage — and deletes the justifying comment with it.
findings.short_summary: Buffer/base64 wrap of UUID nonce is unnecessary

findings.summary: `img-src 'self' data: blob:` has no https: source, so standard markdown images (`![alt](https://…)`) in LLM-generated output rendered by ReactMarkdown/LatexRenderer show as broken-image placeholders.
findings.failure_scenario: The model emits a figure URL in a semiformal output; the user sees a broken image plus a console CSP violation, content-dependent and silent. Decide deliberately: add `https:` to img-src, or document remote images as intentionally blocked.
findings.short_summary: img-src blocks remote images in LLM markdown output

findings.summary: No decision record in docs/decisions/ for the CSP approach, though CLAUDE.md requires one for significant architectural choices and the repo has eight ADRs for comparably scoped decisions.
findings.failure_scenario: The 'strict-dynamic' trust model, the style-src 'unsafe-inline' carve-out, and the static-rendering trade-off live only in file comments (which this branch has already had to fix once for going stale, b25e939); the next rename or refactor evaporates the security reasoning. Add docs/decisions/NNN-csp-nonces.md.
findings.short_summary: No ADR in docs/decisions for the CSP architecture

findings.summary: No proxy.test.ts exists (the repo has 24 Vitest test files; CLAUDE.md says to write tests alongside implementation) for behavior that only fails in a real browser — a dropped directive or broken matcher ships invisibly.
findings.failure_scenario: Findings above (response-only CSP, prefetch bypass) pass `npm run build`, lint, and the whole test suite while shipping a blank page. A unit test asserting the same nonce appears in both the forwarded request CSP header and the response header, plus one for the matcher exclusions, makes the design enforced instead of comment-based.
findings.short_summary: No tests for security-critical proxy behavior

findings.summary: CLAUDE.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md were not updated: the directory layout lists no root-level proxy.ts, and layout.tsx's description omits that it now forces dynamic rendering app-wide.
findings.failure_scenario: CLAUDE.md's Documentation Maintenance section requires updating the Architecture/directory docs for project-structure changes; a reader debugging a blocked script finds no mention a CSP layer exists, and someone "cleaning up" layout.tsx's seemingly pointless await re-enables static rendering. Add proxy.ts to the layout docs and note the request path change.
findings.short_summary: CLAUDE.md/ARCHITECTURE.md not updated for new proxy layer

findings.summary: The connect-src rationale comment names OpenAlex, which appears nowhere else in the repository (Anthropic and OpenRouter are real; grep for openalex outside proxy.ts returns nothing).
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer tightening connect-src hunts for an OpenAlex integration that was never built, or preserves an allowance for it on the comment's authority. Name only the services that exist, or state the invariant ("all LLM calls are server-side via /api/*").
findings.short_summary: Comment cites OpenAlex, which doesn't exist in the repo

Review complete — 14 verified findings reported, and one of them is a release blocker.

The headline: the CSP nonce scheme never engages. Next.js reads the nonce from the **request's** `Content-Security-Policy` header (I confirmed this in the installed Next source, `app-render.js:166`), but `proxy.ts` only sets the CSP on the **response**. So no script ever gets a nonce attribute, and because `'strict-dynamic'` makes browsers ignore `'self'`, every one of Next's own bootstrap scripts is blocked — the production app would ship as a dead, never-hydrated shell. The comment in `app/layout.tsx` describes this mechanism backwards, which is what hides the bug. The fix is small: set the built CSP string on the forwarded request headers as well as the response.

Beyond that, verified collateral damage from the policy itself: graph PNG export breaks (`connect-src 'self'` blocks the `fetch(data:)` in `exportGraph.ts`), the prefetch exclusion in the matcher serves documents with *no* CSP at all, and dev mode lacks the `'unsafe-eval'` carve-out Next needs for HMR/the error overlay. Two plausible-but-engine-dependent risks around pdfjs (worker + wasm under `'strict-dynamic'`). Plus cleanups — the dead `x-nonce` header, the unnecessary `Buffer`/base64 wrap, `await headers()` vs `export const dynamic` — and convention gaps (no ADR, no proxy tests, docs not updated, a comment citing a nonexistent OpenAlex integration).

I'd fix the request-header bug and re-verify in a real browser before merging; the full list is in the findings panel.
